# Real Info-ZIP split sets

Split (spanned) ZIP sets written by Info-ZIP, used by `tests/member_map_zip_split.rs` as ground truth for split ZIP
member maps, and by `tests/zip_split_extract.rs`, whose expected listings and contents are 7-Zip 26.06's
(`7z l -slt`, `7z x -ppassword`).

Writer: `zip -v` reports "This is Zip 3.0 (July 5th 2008), by Info-ZIP, with modifications by Apple Inc."
(`/usr/bin/zip` on macOS).

| set | volumes | contents |
|---|---|---|
| `stored.z01`, `stored.z02`, `stored.zip` | 3 | stored (`-0`): `a.bin` (140,000 random bytes, crosses both boundaries), the directory `dir/`, `dir/b.txt` (640 bytes) |
| `deflated.z01`, `deflated.zip` | 2 | deflated: `c.txt` (93,336 bytes of base64, 70,626 packed, crosses the boundary), `dir/b.txt` |
| `crypt.z01`, `crypt.zip` | 2 | ZipCrypto (`-P password`), stored: `s.bin` (66,000 random bytes, crosses the boundary) |

Every first volume starts with the spanning signature `PK\x07\x08`, and offsets in disk 0 count it. The numbered
volumes are exactly 65,536 bytes: data is cut at the byte, mid-member. The central directory and end record are in
the `.zip`. Plain entries have no data descriptor; the encrypted entry has one (flags `0x0009`), so its ZipCrypto
check byte is the high byte of the DOS time.

Commands (inputs from Python's seeded generator; the random bytes are checked by their CRCs, not regenerated by the
tests):

```sh
mkdir -p in/dir && cd in
python3 -I -c "
import random, base64
r = random.Random(7)
open('a.bin', 'wb').write(bytes(r.getrandbits(8) for _ in range(140000)))
open('dir/b.txt', 'wb').write(b'hello split zip\n' * 40)
open('c.txt', 'wb').write(base64.b64encode(bytes(r.getrandbits(8) for _ in range(70000))))
open('s.bin', 'wb').write(bytes(r.getrandbits(8) for _ in range(66000)))
"
touch -t 202601020304.05 a.bin dir/b.txt c.txt s.bin dir
mkdir ../out
zip -q -X -0 -s 64k ../out/stored.zip a.bin dir dir/b.txt
zip -q -X -s 64k ../out/deflated.zip c.txt dir/b.txt
zip -q -X -0 -P password -s 64k ../out/crypt.zip s.bin
```

The ZipCrypto encryption header is random, so rerunning the commands gives a different `crypt` set.
